html:
The Eastern Shoshone are the Shoshone of western Wyoming and the nearby corner of Utah and Idaho. They speak a Numic language of the Uto-Aztecan family.

Unlike the Western Shoshone of the Great Basin, they took up the horse early, around 1700, and with it the bison hunting life of the Great Plains. For a time in the 1700s Shoshone horsemen ranged far onto the northern plains, until the Blackfoot, armed with guns from the fur trade, and smallpox drove them back into the Rockies. Their great leader of the 1800s, Washakie, kept peace with the United States and allied with it against the Lakota and Crow. In the Fort Bridger Treaty of 1868 he secured the Wind River valley as their reservation, which they later had to share with their old enemies the Arapaho.
